about: Quantitative field targets for ChimpBench (docs/realism-design.md §2). Values are as reported by the sources; "accept" is the band the simulation must hit, scaled to ChimpBench communities (12–22 members, 3–7 adult males) where stated. Evidence: H multi-site or large-sample full text; M one site, abstract-only or derived; L secondary, captive or qualitative. role fitted = may be used for calibration; held-out = never used for tuning. encoded = the mechanism was designed from this pattern, so a match is weak evidence.
protocolPolicy: Every protocol parameter (observer settings, classifier rules, metric windows and thresholds, scoring rules) is set from the source's methods text or by validating the instrument against simulation truth, never by looking at a field-target verdict.

The protocol is frozen with a hash (protocolFreeze): sha256 over src/field/*.ts, scripts/lib/field-worker.ts, each target's id, role, encoded flag, band and observer protocol and its verdict-changing flags (compromised, protocolRevisedPostHoc, revisedPostFreeze, tuned, heldAsFail, instrumentWarning, partiallyEncoded, notScorable), the c12Fitted declarations, the comparison code (src/compare/*.ts, scripts/compare-*.ts; since the C7a review) and the scenario scoring scripts (scripts/field-scenario.ts, scripts/c9-scenario.ts; since C9). scripts/field-metrics.ts prints whether the current hash matches.

Any change needs a protocolLog entry: date, parameter, old -> new, reason (source text with page, bug, or truth accuracy), which results had been seen, and verdicts before -> after. A change after the freeze also needs a new freeze hash.

A held-out target touched by a change made after its value was seen is compromised (reported, never counted as validation) unless the change is a bug fix or follows the source's methods text and was made before the freeze; those are flagged protocolRevisedPostHoc and reported with before/after values. After the freeze, any change that touches a held-out target compromises it.
A fitted target whose protocol was changed after its value was seen without such a reason reverts to the source value.
Instrument validation against truth (sampling accuracy, classifier precision and recall) is allowed at any time, because truth is not a field target; each validation run is logged.
